done_when: forge next says an item whose pull request merged is merged and names the cleanup, instead of waiting for checks, and a test proves it

findings.body: When the last task merges on GitHub but origin/<default> has not been fetched, the new GitHub-derived status reaches this branch and recommends `forge story done`. That command still reads the last-fetched ref (`src/forge/story.py:174` and `:376–381`) and refuses completion when a task's merge is absent (`src/forge/story.py:182–186`). Removing the worktrees does not refresh that ref, so following the printed instructions produces a contradictory “not merged yet” refusal. Include a fetch before the story-completion command when merge evidence comes only from GitHub.
findings.title: Fetch merged task state before recommending story completion

why: forge next lists already-merged fixes and tasks as waiting for their checks while their worktrees still exist
